record.original_question: Prove that the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equation admits wandering solutions.

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Prove that the 3D Euler equation has wandering solutions. The only type of results in this direction are the non-transitivity and non-mixing properties of the 3D Euler equations proved using the ideas of the KAM theory; see [72]. It turns out that the dynamical system defined by the hydrodynamical Euler equation on any closed Riemannian 3-manifold M is not mixing in the C k topology (for k > 4 and non-integer) for any prescribed value of helicity and sufficiently large energy. Furthermore, this non-mixing property of the flow of the 3D Euler equation has a local nature: in any neighbourhood of a “typical” steady solution on S3 there is a generic set of initial conditions such that the corresponding Euler flows will never enter a vicinity (in the C k norm for any non-integer k > 10) of the original steady flow; see [73]. Along the way one constructs a family of functionals on the space of divergence-free C 1 vector fields on M which are integrals of motion of the 3D Euler equation: given a vector field these functionals measure the part of the manifold M foliated by ergodic invariant tori of fixed isotopy types. The KAM theory allows one to establish certain continuity properties of these functionals in the C k -topology and to get a lower bound on the C k -distance between a divergence-free field (in particular, a steady solution) and a trajectory of the Euler flow. This way one obtains an obstruction for the mixing under the Euler flow of C k -neighbourhoods of divergence-free vector fields on M . The local version of non-mixing is based on a similar KAM-type argument to generate knotted invariant tori from elliptic orbits in nondegenerate steady Euler flows.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold, and consider the incompressible Euler equation
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
for a time-dependent divergence-free vector field $u(t,\cdot)$ on $M$, tangent to $\partial M$ if any. For a fixed regularity class (e.g. $C^k$ with non-integer $k$ sufficiently large, or a suitable Sobolev space) on the space $\mathcal{X}$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, call a solution $u(t,\cdot)$ a wandering solution if there exists an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathcal{X}$ of the initial datum $u(0,\cdot)$ and a time $T>0$ such that $u(t,\cdot)\notin U$ for all $t\ge T$ (equivalently, the trajectory eventually leaves a neighborhood of its initial datum and never returns).

Prove that the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on some closed Riemannian 3-manifold $M$ admits a wandering solution in this sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally regarded as open. Only partial results are available: using KAM-theoretic methods, Khesin, Kuksin and Peralta-Salas (and subsequent work) established non-mixing and non-transitivity of the 3D Euler flow in suitable C^k topologies for prescribed helicity and large energy, both globally and locally near typical steady states on S^3. These results constitute the only known progress toward the existence of wandering solutions in 3D, analogous to the 2D results of Nadirashvili and Shnirelman, but a direct construction of wandering solutions for the 3D Euler equation has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: KAM theory and the 3D Euler equation
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes non-mixing of the 3D Euler equation via KAM theory; viewed as a 3D analogue of Nadirashvili/Shnirelman wandering solutions in 2D.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (non-mixing) results are known toward wandering solutions in 3D.

status_evidence.title: Global, local and dense non-mixing of the 3D Euler equation
status_evidence.snippet: Proves global, local and dense non-mixing properties for the 3D Euler equation, extending earlier KAM-based results.
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward wandering solutions consists of non-mixing theorems, not a direct construction.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open problem to prove that the 3D Euler equation has wandering solutions, citing non-mixing results as the only progress.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of wandering solutions for 3D Euler is stated as an open problem.
